items.descriptionAdvanced: Borj el Kebir is an imposing 15th-century fortress in the town of Houmt Souk, originally raised to defend the island of Djerba against frequent pirate raids. The monumental coastal structure is an important example of Hafsid architecture, with walls that were further enhanced in the 16th century by the famous corsair Dragut. Today, the fortress stands as one of the island's most significant historical attractions, vividly demonstrating the vital importance of maritime defense strategy in medieval North Africa.
factsAdvanced: Fortress was constructed in the 15th century.
Hafsid dynasty built it to defend the island.
Dragut, the feared corsair, conquered it in the 16th century.
One of the central monuments of the town of Houmt Souk.
Walls follow the techniques of naval military architecture of the era.
Historically was the most important defensive bastion of the island.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Great Mosque of Sousse is one of the oldest and most distinctive examples of Islamic architecture in North Africa, built in 851. Its fortress-like design, massive walls, and the lack of a minaret give the building a unique character, reflecting the strict and functional architectural approach of the early centuries of Islamic conquest. The mosque is situated in the historical center of Sousse and remains one of the city's most important religious and cultural legacies, providing the medina with its peaceful yet imposing atmosphere.
factsAdvanced: Construction of the mosque was completed in 851.
Unlike most mosques, no minaret was built here.
Fortress-like style indicates early Islamic defensive architecture.
One of the most defining historical buildings of the Sousse medina.
Architectural solutions follow principles of austerity and simplicity.
Principal religious building in the historic center of the city.

items.descriptionAdvanced: Dar Ben Abdallah is a traditional late 18th-century residential building in the heart of the Tunis medina, showcasing the sophistication and decoration of the city's bourgeois architecture of the era. The palace's rich interior décor, including Andalusian-style tiles and detailed wood carvings, attests to the prosperity and artistic standards of its owners at the time. Today it functions as the Regional Museum of Art and Popular Traditions, where visitors can gain insight into the history of the social and cultural life of the city and the region.
factsAdvanced: Palace was constructed at the end of the 18th century.
Today functions as a regional museum of art and popular traditions.
Andalusian-influenced tiles are among the palace's most beautiful decorations.
Wood carvings are outstanding examples of the era's craftsmanship.
Historical representative of the social and cultural life of Tunis.
One of the city's most significant museum buildings.

items.descriptionAdvanced: Dar Othman is one of the most famous historical mansions in Tunis from the end of the 16th century, built for Dey Othman in the central part of the medina. The building is one of the finest examples of the era, attracting attention with its black-and-white marble facade and refined Andalusian-style decorations. The interior design of the palace and the architectural elements used reflect the demanding tastes of the political elite of the time, preserving the historical elegance of the city until today.
factsAdvanced: Erected at the end of the 16th century.
Known as the residence of Dey Othman.
Its black-and-white marble facade is unique.
Andalusian influences define the decorations.
One of the treasures of the medina's architectural heritage.
Palace represents the lifestyle of the political and social elite.

items.descriptionAdvanced: The Mosque of the Barber (Zaouia Sidi Sahab) is a unique religious complex and one of the most famous places of pilgrimage in Kairouan. The building preserves the tomb of one of the Prophet's companions, and its interior spaces are decorated with an astonishing richness of Andalusian-style ceramic tiles and fine stucco work. The zaouia complex, which underwent major modifications in the 17th century, is important not only for its religious significance but also for its artistic execution, standing as one of the most vital creations of Islamic art in North Africa.
factsAdvanced: Mosque built around the tomb of one of the Prophet's famous companions.
Gained its current form during 17th-century modifications.
Characterized by rich ceramic and stucco decorations with Andalusian influences.
One of the most important places of pilgrimage in Kairouan.
Zaouia complex is the center of religious and architectural heritage.
Decorations are masterpieces of Islamic decorative art.
